subject.title: RFC 0009: align Hosted Feed v1 specifications

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this branch's Hosted Feed v1 contract—including strict DSSE trust binding, publisher projections, signed scalable distribution, and client-first watches—as the normative implementation target?
rationale: The RFC changes public protocol and trust semantics across two repositories; source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers want this exact v1 boundary, rollout order, or compatibility commitment.

options.title: Adopt the v1 contract
options.body: Accept this normative boundary, then update the RFC lifecycle metadata and require the linked producer/consumer lanes to demonstrate the accepted interoperability contract.

options.title: Keep it as a draft
options.body: Leave the branch open while protocol owners narrow or revise the trust, query, delta, and watch requirements before acceptance.

options.title: Split the contract
options.body: Accept only the base feed and trust contract now, while moving scalable projections and watches to separately approved addenda.

recommendation.title: Adopt the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept this normative boundary, then update the RFC lifecycle metadata and require the linked producer/consumer lanes to demonstrate the accepted interoperability contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior substantive review history on the hosted-feed architecture makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the product-boundary decision.
